title: Choosing a scent diffuser for hospitality spaces
summary: Start with the space, the airflow and the way your team will manage the equipment.

sections.title: Start with a practical brief
sections.text: A hotel entrance, a reception lounge and a guest corridor serve different purposes. Describe the intended space before choosing a machine. Share the floor area, ceiling height, opening hours and the locations of doors, ventilation outlets and seating. This gives the supplier a useful starting point for a model discussion. A coverage figure in a catalog should be treated as one selection input, rather than a promise that every room will behave identically.

sections.title: Choose an installation your team can manage
sections.text: The KWS catalog includes different installation arrangements. Check the exact model for its power supply, refill capacity and mounting requirements. Consider who will refill the equipment, how easily they can reach it, and whether an electrical outlet is available. An accessible service location is often more useful than hiding a machine in a place that is difficult to maintain.

sections.title: Review a sample in the intended environment
sections.text: Ask about a sample and a fragrance suitable for the selected machine. Begin with the supplier’s operating instructions and make adjustments through the approved controls. Invite the team responsible for the space to review the result at different times of day. Confirm the quotation, lead time and product-specific documentation before ordering.

title: Standalone or HVAC scent diffusion?
summary: Compare installation arrangements before comparing product names.

sections.title: Two different installation conversations
sections.text: A standalone device and a machine intended for HVAC integration have different placement and setup considerations. Start by identifying whether the project needs a device in a room or a proposed connection to an air-handling system. KWS lists several diffuser families; the product detail page is the place to check the information for the exact model.

sections.title: Bring the building team into the discussion
sections.text: For an HVAC proposal, involve the person responsible for the ventilation system. Share the system arrangement, operating schedule and proposed equipment location with the supplier. Confirm connection requirements and installation instructions before purchase. A product name containing “HVAC” does not replace a project-specific installation review.

sections.title: Compare operation as well as purchase price
sections.text: Refill access, power availability, control settings and maintenance arrangements all affect daily use. Compare these details alongside capacity and dimensions. If the required arrangement is unclear, send a drawing or a short project brief to KWS and ask which models should be considered. Confirm the final equipment and installation scope in writing.

title: A practical guide to touchless soap dispensers
summary: Check refill compatibility, power and installation together.

sections.title: Choose around the washroom routine
sections.text: A dispenser should suit the people using the facility and the staff maintaining it. Think about the intended mounting position, access for refilling and the expected daily pattern of use. Product capacity is only one part of the decision. The KWS catalog provides model-specific fields for comparing available equipment.

sections.title: Confirm the refill and power arrangement
sections.text: Do not assume every dispenser accepts the same liquid or has the same power supply. Confirm the approved refill type, the model’s power requirements and any installation instructions. Ask for a demonstration or sample when the operating behavior is important to the project. Keep the product identifier in your inquiry so that the reply applies to the selected item.

sections.title: Plan for cleaning and support
sections.text: Agree who will check refill levels, clean the exterior and follow the operating instructions. Record the model and retain the supplier’s documentation. If a dispenser behaves differently from expected, describe the power arrangement, refill and visible symptoms when contacting support. Avoid opening or modifying a unit unless the supplier’s instructions authorize that procedure.

title: Matching paper dispensers with the right refill
summary: Paper format and service access matter as much as the dispenser finish.

sections.title: Check the format before selecting the cabinet
sections.text: The paper dispenser category includes different formats and product arrangements. Start with the type of paper the facility intends to purchase. Confirm the refill dimensions and the dispenser’s supported format with the supplier. Similar-looking cabinets are not necessarily interchangeable, and a catalog photograph cannot confirm every refill detail.

sections.title: Consider the staff’s service routine
sections.text: Think about how the dispenser will be opened, checked and refilled. Choose a mounting position that supports the intended use while allowing the cleaning team to reach the unit. Confirm the product dimensions and installation method on the exact model page. Include the available wall space in a quotation request if it is limited.

sections.title: Validate the combination with a sample
sections.text: Where the refill format is important, test the proposed paper with a sample dispenser before a larger purchase. Review dispensing behavior and service access using the supplied instructions. Agree the product code, compatible refill and replacement arrangements in writing. A clear record makes repeat ordering easier for both the customer and supplier.

title: What to include in an OEM / ODM project brief
summary: A clear brief helps turn a first inquiry into a useful product discussion.

sections.title: Describe the requirement before the customization
sections.text: Begin with the intended application, product family, target quantity and preferred schedule. Identify any catalog models that are close to the requirement. Explain what needs to change and what can remain standard. This allows the supplier to distinguish a product selection inquiry from a development or customization request.

sections.title: Make the requested changes specific
sections.text: Where branding, color, packaging or other changes are needed, provide the relevant artwork or written requirements. Ask the supplier to confirm which options are available for the selected model. Do not assume every product supports every customization. Samples, approval steps and any development costs should be included in the written discussion.

sections.title: Close the approval loop
sections.text: Agree which sample or specification will be used as the ordering reference. Confirm product identifiers, quantities, packaging, documentation and commercial terms before production. Keep change requests in a single revision record. The KWS team can discuss OEM / ODM requirements; the confirmed quotation defines the scope for a particular order.

title: Fragrance refills: confirm compatibility first
summary: Match the refill to the device and follow the supplied instructions.

sections.title: Treat the machine and fragrance as a combination
sections.text: The KWS product range includes fragrance equipment and essential oil products. Before ordering a refill, identify the exact diffuser model and the intended fragrance product. Ask the supplier to confirm compatibility and the instructions for that combination. A product category name alone does not establish that every liquid can be used in every machine.

sections.title: Keep the operating instructions close at hand
sections.text: Review filling, storage and operating guidance supplied with the selected product. Follow any product-specific labeling and documentation. Do not mix refills or substitute a liquid solely because its appearance is similar. If documentation is missing or unclear, request it before use.

sections.title: Keep repeat orders easy to identify
sections.text: Record the fragrance name or code, the machine model and the supplier’s confirmed refill details. Include those identifiers in later inquiries so that a replacement can be checked against the previous order. When considering a new fragrance, discuss a sample and review it in the intended setting before confirming a larger purchase.

title: Before a scent project: a simple site survey
summary: Gather the information that makes a supplier conversation more productive.

sections.title: Make a picture of the space
sections.text: A useful site brief combines a simple plan with a few photographs. Mark the areas under consideration, entrances, ventilation points, nearby power outlets and possible equipment positions. Add the approximate dimensions and operating hours. The goal is to make the intended environment understandable to the supplier, rather than to create a complex engineering document.

sections.title: Explain the operating conditions
sections.text: Describe how the area is used during the day and who will look after the equipment. Note access restrictions, service times and any building requirements. For a proposed HVAC arrangement, involve the building’s ventilation team and ask the supplier what additional system information is needed.

sections.title: Use the brief to confirm a proposal
sections.text: Send the information with the product inquiry and request a model discussion. Check the proposed installation, refill arrangement and ongoing service needs. Use a sample or a supplier-approved review process where appropriate. Keep the agreed scope with the quotation so that everyone is working from the same project description.

title: Building a simple equipment care routine
summary: A clear record helps your team maintain equipment and describe support questions.

sections.title: Create a model-specific routine
sections.text: Keep the product instructions available to the people responsible for each device. Record the model, installation location and refill information. Use the supplier’s guidance to define refill checks, exterior cleaning and any routine tasks. A general checklist is useful for organizing work, but it should not replace instructions for the actual product.

sections.title: Report a problem with useful details
sections.text: When asking for support, include the product identifier, the circumstances in which the issue appears and any visible indicators. Photographs or a short video can help explain the behavior. Note the power and refill arrangement where relevant. This gives the supplier a clearer basis for advising the next step.

sections.title: Confirm service terms for the order
sections.text: Ask about warranty and support arrangements before purchase and keep the confirmed terms with the order records. Installation conditions, applicable documentation and permitted maintenance steps may differ by model. Follow the supplier’s instructions and agree any repair or replacement arrangements before taking action.
